We observe that the Change in Law provisions were incorporated to the Bid documents by amendment No.8 dated 28.11.2020, whereas the last date of submissions of bid was 7.12.2020(online) and 9.12.2020 (offline). Therefore, it does not appear to be a case that such provisions have been introduced after the closure of the bid and thus, bidder(s) participating in the bid were made aware about the said provisions. The Change in Law Rules have been framed to facilitate timely recovery of costs due to Change in Law events and to provide a process and methodology to be followed. As per the provisions of the Change in Law Rules, on occurrence of a Change in Law, the affected party (generator) and other parties (procurers) are to settle the Change in Law claims among themselves and approach the Commission only in terms of Rule 3(8) of the Change in Law Rules. 50.
